coupled_content: Juice purges; plant body checks evacuation by drying.
For evacuation, serve cabbage together with cooking water and oil/fish sauce or salt; avoid excessive boiling to retain juice.
For drying a moist belly, pour off first water, immediately use other hot water and boil again until soft.
Longer boiling loses more juice; the entry says no boiling preserves all juice.
Air or cold-water contact is prohibited for the twice-boiled material and said to defeat proper softening even with prolonged boiling.
The later former/that-water instruction resumes the earlier branch rather than unconditionally adding a third boil.
Similar drying is compatible with different nourishment; eye-condition exception and uncertain urinary effect constrain scope.
Ancient versus current name usage distinguishes one historical name from invariant plant identity.
